implemented.name: getCurrentAdminStatus
implemented.notes: Answers from the authoritative admins/{oid} registry record (not token claims — strictly harder to spoof than the source). Returns the source response shape incl. the permissions array the frontend gates UI on. A 200 is an ANSWER (isAdmin true or false because the registry was read); a 401 or 500 is a check that could not run, and the frontend must render those as 'unknown' rather than as a denial (#503) — requireUser denies only with 401, so a non-200 here is never an authorization verdict. The isAdmin:false answer also carries canBootstrap, the server's own verdict on whether bootstrapCurrentUserAdmin would succeed, so the UI offers that button only when it would work and never to an account that already has a registry row.

implemented.name: getAuthExpectations
implemented.notes: Since #515 every guarded route additionally requires the delegated scope `access_as_admin` in `scp`, and the verifier asserts `tid`, `iss`/`tid` agreement and `ver == 2.0`; the v1 `sts.windows.net` issuer is no longer accepted. A token with no `scp` (an ID token) is a 401 with a `missing-scope` audit row. Since #519 it also reports `requiredScope`, `requiredTokenVersion` and `labAgentAppRole`, each read from the guard's own constant rather than a copy, and the Integrations page renders them beside the credential inventory. Admin → Diagnostics (#355): the values the guard actually enforces — { expectedAudience: ENTRA_API_AUDIENCE, tenantId: ENTRA_TENANT_ID, adminAppRole: 'Admin', registryContainer: 'admins' } — so the page can compare the token it decodes in the browser against the API as deployed rather than against a frontend constant. requireUser, not requireRole, because the caller being diagnosed may hold the App Role and be missing from the registry. Discloses nothing a valid token does not already carry.

implemented.name: publerProxy
implemented.implementation: lib/integrations/rest-proxy.js — authenticated pass-through to Publer at https://app.publer.com/api/v1, credentialed from PUBLER_API_KEY + PUBLER_WORKSPACE_ID. The caller supplies {path, method, body}; assertSafePath is the security boundary, rejecting absolute URLs, protocol-relative paths, schemes, '..' segments, backslashes and control characters, because a credentialed proxy with a caller-chosen path is a confused deputy and the gate in front is 'editor', not 'admin'. Upstream status and body are passed through so the admin page can show the real error. An unseeded key returns 200 with ok:false and INTEGRATION_NOT_CONFIGURED, which the Connections page renders as not-connected.

implemented.name: linkieProxy

The caller supplies {path, method, body}; assertSafePath is the security boundary, rejecting absolute URLs, protocol-relative paths, schemes, '..' segments, backslashes and control characters, because a credentialed proxy with a caller-chosen path is a confused deputy and the gate in front is 'editor', not 'admin'. Upstream status and body are passed through so the admin page can show the real error. An unseeded key returns 200 with ok:false and INTEGRATION_NOT_CONFIGURED, which the Connections page renders as not-connected. Additionally allowlisted to the endpoints the admin page calls — /profiles, /analytics/traffic-stats and the profile-scoped posts routes — because the API key's scopes are broader than any one screen needs. Base URL and allowlist taken from Site-Main functions/cms/proxies.js rather than inferred.

implemented.name: connectionProbe
implemented.implementation: lib/integrations/connection-probe.js — the Integrations page's connection test for the services whose credentials are read only on the server: Telegram (GET /bot<token>/getMe), RSS.com (GET https://api.rss.com/v4/podcasts), YouTube (GET youtube/v3/search, maxResults=1), Resend (GET https://api.resend.com/domains, which a sending-access-only key is refused, so a pass proves the key can manage contacts and broadcasts), Qlty (GET https://api.qlty.sh/user, #569), Replicate (GET https://api.replicate.com/v1/account, ADR 0033) and Firecrawl (GET https://api.firecrawl.dev/v1/team/credit-usage, ADR 0033) — the last two read-only and free, so the AI-key cards on Integrations have a test that spends nothing. Entra editor-gated. UNLIKE the REST proxies, the caller supplies only a NAME — {probe:'telegram'|'rsscom'|'youtube'|'resend'|'qlty'|'replicate'|'firecrawl'} — and the URL, method and headers are built server-side from a frozen table, so there is no caller-supplied component in the outbound request at all rather than a validated one. Telegram and YouTube authenticate in the URL, so the upstream response is redacted before it is parsed and the built URL is never returned or logged. Only Telegram records a key verdict (getMe takes the token alone and answers 401 for a bad one); RSS.com's 401/403 split is unmeasured, YouTube answers 403 for an exceeded quota as well as a bad key, Resend refuses a sending-only key as well as a wrong one, a Qlty 403 could be a token scope, and neither Replicate's nor Firecrawl's 401/403 split has been measured, so none of those six turns a light red. The YouTube probe costs ~100 of 10,000 daily quota units, which is why it is a button and never a timer. An unseeded key returns 200 with ok:false and INTEGRATION_NOT_CONFIGURED.

implemented.name: createContentFromRecording
implemented.implementation: lib/content/draft-from-recording.js — one recording transcript into a content draft. Validates {recordingId, contentType ∈ blog_post|technical_guide|linkedin_post|podcast_notes|meeting_summary, title?, transcript?, provider?}; reads recordings/{id} (404 when absent), takes the transcript from the body or the stored recording (422 under 200 chars, 413 over 400k), infers 'Cloud Provider' from title+transcript with the URL drafter's keyword map, then one createDrafter().generateDraft call — the same drafter as generateArticleDraft/forge, feature-gated as forgeDrafting, with the content type's instruction block as customInstructionPrompt — and persists through createContentDocument, the createContentItem write path (dedup 409, quality gate, document shape; critique deferred to review). Patches the recording to status 'routed' with contentId/routedAt server-side so the link survives a client that dies before its own PATCH. Editor-gated; 75 s budget under the client's 90 s timeout; errors 400/404/413/422 input, 409/422 from persistence, 503 AI disabled or unconfigured, 504 budget, 502 generation. The request's provider hint is recorded as requestedAiProvider, never honoured as routing — the router's configured order decides and aiProvider records what ran. Response { ok, contentId, draft: { title, summary, keyTopics, aiProvider, cloudProvider } }.

GET returns issue.etag. GET's issue carries preheader (empty when unset); renderIssue emits it as the hidden inbox-preview block at the top of the email body, so approve sends it. PATCH accepts only {customNote (<=2000), subject (1-120), preheader (<=150, whitespace collapsed; empty clears it), sections, etag} on a draft; any other field is 400. sections may only remove items, reorder items within a section, reorder sections or remove whole sections: each submitted section is matched to a stored one by id and each item to a stored item in that section by url, any other field sent must equal the stored value, duplicates are refused, and the STORED items are written in the submitted order; an added, moved or edited item or section, or an issue left with no items, is 400 SECTIONS_INVALID; itemCount is recomputed. etag is REQUIRED (400 ETAG_REQUIRED without it), an etag that is not the stored one is 409 ISSUE_CHANGED before any write, the replace itself is ETag-conditional, and the response carries the new etag. DELETE (editor) takes body {etag} REQUIRED; only a draft or rejected issue, otherwise 409; it writes status deleted with deletedAt/deletedBy through an ETag-conditional replace, so it cannot race an approval that already claimed the issue, and answers {ok, id}. A deleted issue is a 404 on every route and is rebuilt from scratch by the builder. Issue ids are issue-YYYY-MM-DD; anything else is a 404 before Cosmos is read. When Newsletter settings name a Resend template (templateId, #557), every response that carries a preview renders it in that template (lib/newsletter/template-layout.js: the body at {{{NEWSLETTER_BODY}}}, escaped subject/preheader/period markers, the postal address and {{{RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL}}} appended when the template lacks them), fetched through GET /templates/{id} with a 5-minute in-process cache per id (template-source.js). A template that cannot be fetched or used, or RESEND_API_KEY unset, gives the built-in design plus templateProblem {code, message}; templateProblem is null otherwise.

PUBLISHER: it emails every confirmed subscriber. Body {etag} REQUIRED (400 ETAG_REQUIRED); then 503 NEWSLETTER_SENDING_DISABLED, before any read or Resend call, unless NEWSLETTER_SENDING_ENABLED is exactly "true" (Terraform newsletter_sending_enabled, default false; GET reports it as sendingEnabled); an etag that is not the stored one is 409 ISSUE_CHANGED, so an issue edited after the approver opened it is not sent. 409 SETTINGS_INCOMPLETE until the postal address and reply-to are saved; 503 without RESEND_API_KEY; 409 unless a draft. The send slot and the rendered email are worked out BEFORE the claim (409 SETTINGS_INVALID if the slot cannot be), so nothing on the site's side can strand an issue in sending. Claims the issue draft -> sending with an ETag-conditional replace before calling Resend, so simultaneous approvals create one broadcast. Creates the broadcast to the Newsletter segment from newsletter@news.hybridcloudworks.com with send:true and scheduled_at at the configured slot (DST-correct), or immediately when that slot is more than 72 h away. The outcome is written only while the issue is still the claim: success -> scheduled or sent with broadcastId; a Resend refusal -> draft with lastError and approval cleared, 502; no answer from Resend at all (timeout) -> stays sending with lastError, 502 SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, because a broadcast may exist; accepted but not recorded -> 200 with the usual issue payload (re-read, so it shows sending) plus warning; logs carry the invocation id and an error's name and code only, never issue or broadcast ids or SDK messages; a reject that landed mid-send stands and the answer is 409 CHANGED_DURING_SEND naming the broadcast. A process that dies mid-send leaves sending, never retried automatically. With a Resend template chosen in Newsletter settings (#557), the broadcast html is the issue merged into that template; if the template cannot be fetched or used, approval is refused with 409 TEMPLATE_UNUSABLE (and templateProblem) after the send-slot check and BEFORE the claim, so nothing is claimed or sent in a design other than the one chosen. The plain text is always the built-in rendering.

ADR 0033 Amplify slice. PUBLISHER. Cancels a scheduled issue: Resend's only cancel for a scheduled broadcast is DELETE /broadcasts/{id}, which this calls; a refusal is 502 CANCEL_REFUSED carrying Resend's own sentence (plan or state), and nothing is written. On success the issue returns to a kept draft (savedAt kept or set, canceledAt, canceledBroadcastId; broadcastId, scheduledAt and approval cleared), approvable again. Body {etag} REQUIRED; 409 unless scheduled with a broadcastId; stale is 409 ISSUE_CHANGED.

ADR 0033 Amplify slice. PUBLISHER. Body {etag, scheduledAt} (ISO, at least a minute ahead; 400 otherwise). Resend's update takes no scheduled_at, so the current broadcast is deleted and a new one created at the new time from the same rendered content (409 TEMPLATE_UNUSABLE first when the chosen template cannot be used). If the delete is refused nothing moves (502 CANCEL_REFUSED, Resend's sentence); if the new broadcast is refused the issue becomes a draft with lastError naming Resend's reason (502 RESCHEDULE_REFUSED). Success writes broadcastId, scheduledAt, sendAt and rescheduledAt; a 412 after the new broadcast exists is 409 CHANGED_DURING_RESCHEDULE naming the broadcast.

ADR 0033 Amplify slice. PUBLISHER. A failed issue (one the reconcile marked: Resend canceled or lost its broadcast) back to a kept draft for a fresh approval; broadcastId, scheduledAt, sentAt and approval cleared, failedBroadcastId and retriedAt recorded, lastError kept for the page. Body {etag} REQUIRED; 409 unless failed.

A new kept draft with the source's subject, preheader, intro, note and sections under today's id (issue-YYYY-MM-DD, or issue-YYYY-MM-DD-n when today's is taken; the id pattern allows the suffix everywhere), duplicatedFrom naming the source. No body. Answers the new issue presented as GET does.

Asks Resend where every scheduled (or sending) issue with a broadcastId stands and writes what it says (lib/newsletter/reconcile.js): sent -> sent with Resend's sent_at; scheduled -> scheduledAt refreshed; queued -> broadcastStatus; canceled or a 404 -> failed with lastError. Every write is ETag-conditional. Answers {ok, reconciled, changed[], warnings[]}. The same reconcile runs lazily on GET of a scheduled issue and on the list for overdue scheduled rows (at most 5 per list read), which is the only path a scheduled issue has to sent. Not under cms/newsletters/{id}: a literal segment there would read as an id. 503 without RESEND_API_KEY.

The From address every send uses — confirmation emails, test sends and broadcasts — with the code constant (HybridCloudWorks <newsletter@news.hybridcloudworks.com>) as the default. GET is editor: {ok, from, isDefault, defaultFrom, sendingDomain, updatedAt, updatedBy}. PUT is PUBLISHER, body {from}: empty returns to the default; otherwise it must parse as an address or 'Name <address>' (400) and sit on the default's domain or a domain Resend lists as verified (400 DOMAIN_NOT_SENDING with the reason, Resend's own when Resend refused the listing). endpoints.implementation: same module, forge; editor; body { ids[] }. A job write that fails reverts the claim to queued (best effort; the list's reconcile reads a forging entry with no job document as failed) and names that entry and the later ones in `notStarted`. (<= 300) } }, dates ISO 8601 with seconds and a zone, and checkedAt, statusTokenRotatedAt and templatePushedAt no more than 10 minutes ahead of the site's clock; anything else is 400 with a sentence, before any read. A statusToken must match ^[A-Za-z0-9]{10}-[A-Za-z0-9]{22}$ (Coder v2.38's key shape) and pass three reads made with it through coder-status.js's guarded GET (verifyStatusToken), each answering exactly 200: GET /api/v2/workspaces?q=status:running with an integer count; GET /api/v2/users/me with username CODER_STATUS_USER (default hcw-status); GET /api/v2/users/me/keys/{id} whose scopes hold template:read, workspace:read and api_key:read and nothing beyond them and user:read (an unscoped key, coder:all or a deprecated scope of all, is refused). Only then is it written to CODER-STATUS-TOKEN by writeCatalogSecret, the Keys tab's own writer (set-only vault PUT, best-effort reference refresh, secret_state lastWriteBy lab-agent:<agentId>, one secret's record at a time under the state document's ETag), with one admin_audit_logs row coder_status_token_rotated (no value). A token that fails a check is 422 { ok: false, stored: false, error } with the check named, a vault refusal 502; the report is recorded either way, with the reason as lastError and the report's statusTokenRotatedAt and statusTokenExpiresAt dropped. Once the vault has the token the answer is 200 { ok: true, stored: true } even when a later step fails, with that failure as lastError. The report is merged into admin_config/coder_automation under its ETag (createDoc, then replaceDocIfMatch, retried on 409/412): event fields keep their stored values when absent, checkedAt, lastError, reportedAt and agentId are replaced, statusTokenRotatedAt is the server's time when a token was stored, and anything in lastError shaped like a Coder key is replaced. signalrOption.fitAssessment: 20 connections is ample for a single-operator admin. The 20k/day cap is the constraint: a 1 msg/sec stream exhausts it in ~5.5h, so it only fits EVENT-DRIVEN pushes (Cosmos change feed -> Functions output binding -> push on actual data change), never chatty streams.
cautions: Free -> Standard scaling incurs downtime: the public IP changes, 30-60 min DNS propagation
Standard_S1 (~$49/unit/month) is a third of the USD 150 platform ceiling and is NOT justified by one admin's dashboard
no SLA means the realtime layer can degrade with no recourse - polling fallback must remain in the client regardless
signalrOption.adoptionTrigger: only if polling proves sluggish in practice; ship polling first
